text:
Casey Mittelstadt has had a strange, productive first two months in Boston's lineup: 8 goals in 23 games while playing what Boston Hockey Now called a shutdown role, on about 14 minutes a night. NBC Sports Boston and CLNS are already asking what his hot start means for his future with the club.

The answer depends on how much of it lasts, and the shooting won't. He has 8 goals on 4.7 expected, shooting 27% against a likely range of 13 to 19%, and Boston has scored 6.4 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice. His top shot speed sits in the 14th percentile; these are placement goals, and placement runs hot and cold.

The defensive job is the better story. At 5v5 the Bruins take 55% of the expected goals with him on, even while getting only 48% of the shot attempts, which says the chances against are small ones. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking liked his passing last season (81st percentile in primary shot assists). Expect the goals to slow and the role to keep him in the lineup.
